samples: This module reads version numbers written as "major.minor.patch" (like 1.4.2) into a checked Version value, and it reports a specific error when the text has the wrong number of parts or a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also prints versions back to text, compares them by major, then minor, then patch, and can pick the latest version from a list (or nothing if the list is empty). It has a compatibility check that accepts a candidate only if it has the same major version and isn't older than the required one. It does not handle pre-release or build suffixes such as "-beta".

This module reads version numbers written as "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a typed version value, and prints them back the same way. It reports a clear error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also compares versions by major, then minor, then patch, checks whether a candidate can stand in for a required version (same major, not older), and picks the latest version from a list. It doesn't handle pre-release or build suffixes.

This module lets you read version numbers written as "major.minor.patch" (for example 1.4.2) into a checked value, print them back, and compare them in order by major, then minor, then patch. Parsing reports a specific error if the text doesn't have exactly three parts or if a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a way to pick the greatest version from a list, but it doesn't handle pre-release or build suffixes like "-beta" or "+build".

This module reads semantic version numbers written as three dot-separated whole numbers (like 1.4.2) into a structured value, prints them back as text, and orders them by major, then minor, then patch. Parsing reports a specific error when the text doesn't have exactly three parts or when a part isn't a non-negative number. It also offers a compatibility check (same major version and not older than the required one) and a way to pick the greatest version from a list, but it doesn't handle pre-release or build suffixes.

This module reads version numbers written as "major.minor.patch" (such as 1.4.2) into a typed version value. It reports a specific error when the text doesn't have exactly three parts or when a part isn't a non-negative whole number. It can also print versions, compare them by major, then minor, then patch, and check whether a candidate can stand in for a required version (same major, not older). It can pick the greatest version from a list, or nothing if the list is empty. It doesn't handle pre-release or build suffixes, so use it only if plain three-part versions are enough.

source.tool: claude -p (Claude Code CLI 2.1.289 (Claude Code), subscription login)

source.thinking: adaptive, cannot be switched off; tokens recorded per session
